chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Time wears out the bodies, renews the hopes, brings death nearer, and distances aspirations. Whoever is successful with it encounters grief, and whoever misses its favours undergoes hardships.

key_terms.الدَّهْرُ: Time / Eternity / The course of life
key_terms.يُخْلِقُ: Wears out / Creates / Forms (in context of aging)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Time wearing out bodies and renewing hopes in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) characterizes al-dahr (time) not merely as a chronological measure but as an active, creative force that simultaneously decays the physical form and revitalizes spiritual or worldly hopes. This duality highlights the transient nature of worldly success, where attaining one's goals often brings the fatigue of maintenance, while missing opportunities breeds enduring regret, reflecting the Shia understanding of life's cyclical trials. The passage serves as a reminder to align one's aspirations with eternal values rather than fleeting temporal gains.
